RegexUtils.match:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns True if the regex pattern matches the beginning of the input text, and False otherwise." match]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: string "The regex pattern to match at the beginning of text."
        <REF> text </REF>: string "The input text to search for the pattern."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True if the pattern matches at the beginning of text; False otherwise."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call re.match(pattern, text) and store the match object or None in ans. RESULT ans]
            [COMMAND If ans is truthy, return True. RESULT True]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: If ans is falsy]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return False. RESULT False]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.findall:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns all non-overlapping matches of the given regular expression pattern in the provided text using Python's re.findall." findall]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: string or compiled regular expression "The regular expression pattern to search for."
        <REF> text </REF>: string or bytes "The input text to scan for matches of the pattern."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> matches </REF>: list "The list of matches returned by re.findall: matched strings if the pattern has no capturing groups, captured strings for one group, tuples of captured strings for multiple groups, or an empty list when no matches are found."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Use re.findall(pattern, text) to find all non-overlapping matches and return the resulting list to the caller. RESULT matches]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.split:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Splits the given text into a list of substrings at every match of the given regular expression pattern and returns that list." split]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: str "Regular expression pattern used to split text."
        <REF> text </REF>: str "Input string to be split."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list "List of substrings produced by splitting text at each occurrence of pattern."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split the text string at every non-overlapping occurrence of pattern using Python's re.split with default maxsplit=0, including captured delimiter groups in the resulting list when present, and return that list. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.sub:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of a regular expression pattern in a string with the given replacement and returns the resulting string." sub]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: str or compiled regex pattern "Regular expression pattern or compiled expression to find in text."
        <REF> replacement </REF>: str or callable "Replacement string, which may contain backreferences, or a callable that receives a match object and returns the replacement string."
        <REF> text </REF>: str "Input string in which all occurrences of pattern are replaced."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: str "The new string produced after replacing all occurrences of pattern; equals text unchanged if no matches are found."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call Python's re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) with the default count of 0 and no flags, replacing every non-overlapping match of pattern in text with replacement. RESULT substituted_text]
            [COMMAND Return substituted_text as the result of the method. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.generate_email_pattern:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates a regular expression pattern for matching common email address formats." generate_email_pattern]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: string "The generated regular expression pattern for email addresses."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Define a raw string constant named pattern containing the regular expression \b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b that matches email addresses. RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Return the value of pattern. RESULT pattern]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.generate_phone_number_pattern:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates a regular expression pattern that matches hyphenated 10-digit phone numbers in the format 123-456-7890." generate_phone_number_pattern]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: string "The regular expression pattern matching a hyphenated 10-digit phone number with word boundaries."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign the raw regular expression string '\b\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}\b' to variable pattern. RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Return the value of variable pattern. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.generate_split_sentences_patt:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates and returns a regular expression pattern that matches sentence-ending punctuation followed by one or two whitespace characters and an uppercase letter, allowing split-sentence logic to preserve the uppercase token." generate_split_sentences_pattern]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> pattern </REF>: str "A raw regular expression string that matches sentence-ending punctuation, one or two whitespace characters, and an uppercase ASCII letter via positive lookahead."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize pattern with the regex constant r'[.!?][\s]{1,2}(?=[A-Z])'. RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Return pattern as the method result. RESULT pattern]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.split_sentences:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Splits the given text into sentences by generating a splitting pattern and passing it with the text to the split helper method." split_sentences]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> text </REF>: text "Input text to split into sentences."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> sentences </REF>: list "List of sentence segments produced from the input text."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Generate the sentence splitting pattern by calling generate_split_sentences_pattern on the current instance. RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Return the result of splitting the input text by calling split with the generated pattern and the text on the current instance. RESULT sentences]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.validate_phone_number:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates a phone number pattern and returns the result of matching the given phone number against it." validate_phone_number]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> phone_number </REF>: string "Phone number to validate."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True if the phone number matches the generated pattern; otherwise False."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Generate the phone number pattern by calling self.generate_phone_number_pattern(). RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Match the generated pattern against phone_number by calling self.match(pattern, phone_number) and return the result. RESULT validation_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
RegexUtils.extract_email:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Generates an email regex pattern and returns all matches found in the input text." extract_email]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> text </REF>: str "The input text in which email addresses are searched."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> email_matches </REF>: list "A list of all email matches found by the regex pattern in the input text."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Generate the email pattern by calling self.generate_email_pattern() and assign the result to pattern. RESULT pattern]
            [COMMAND Call self.findall(pattern, text) with the generated pattern and the original text, then return the resulting list of matches. RESULT email_matches]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
